title: Theo and Poppy's Busy Orchard
markdown:
The sun burst through Theo the bridge builder’s window, golden stripes across the workshop floor. A tingle in his chest. The air hummed with possibility.

“Up and at ’em!” Poppy the dormouse, already a brown blur, whiskers twitching.

Theo stretched. “Morning. What’s the buzz?”

“The orchard. Too quiet.”

They dashed out. Dew sparkled. Apple trees stood tall. Poppy was right. Where were the bees, the butterflies, the clicking beetles? A song missing its notes.

Theo rumbled at a sad bare blossom. “No buzzing visitors.”

Poppy’s ears drooped. “What if the apples don’t grow big and red without our friends to help?”

Ms. Vale ambled by, trowel in hand, blue apron dusted with happy soil. “What’s troubling you this bright morning?”

Theo explained. The empty feel.

Vale smiled wide. She left the my-dears unsaid. “A healthy place needs lots of different living things. They work together.”

She pointed to bright red poppies. “Nectar for the bees. Then the bees go to the apple blossoms. That’s how the apples get their start.”

A tiny red ladybug munched a green leaf — no: munched the little green bugs on it. “She keeps the trees healthier.”

Poppy gasped. “Ladybug helps the tree. Bee helps the apple. They help each other?”

“Every creature has a job. Lots of different plants and animals together — biodiversity.”

Theo tapped his chin. A spark. “Invite more friends for our friends.”

Poppy bounced, tail a blur. “More buzzing, fluttering, scuttling, chirping.”

Theo built tiny bridges over puddles so small bugs could drink without drowning. Poppy, sharp-eyed, planted cheerful sweet-smelling flowers: orange marigolds, yellow daffodils, fragrant thyme. Theo added a miniature bug hotel. They worked in a burst, soil under nails, thyme on their fingers.

The next day paid them. Butterflies twirled. Bees buzzed, legs dusted gold. Beetles scuttled under leaves. Ants marched the new bridges. The orchard hummed.

Vale watched, face glowing, and used the long word once more without wondering what else the world hid. “That mix — biodiversity in action.”

Theo grinned. “A team.”

Poppy, perched on a bright red poppy of her own name, nodded. Happier. Healthier. They did not call today the beginning of amazing discoveries. They counted three bees on one blossom and left the hotel door facing south, where the sun would find it first.
